feedback.problem: Which of the following diagrams represents the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y)=2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(xy)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $∇f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(xy)) \\  & =\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+1} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(xy)) \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+1}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we have to sketch the vector field at the points $(-1,1),$ $(0,-2),$ and $(2,0).$

To sketch the vector field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the expression for $∇f.$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(-1,1) & =\frac{2\cdot 1}{(-1)^{2}(1)^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2\cdot (-1)}{(-1)^{2}(1)^{2}+1}\,j=i-j \\ ∇f(0,-2) & =\frac{2\cdot (-2)}{(0)^{2}(-2)^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2\cdot 0}{(0)^{2}(-2)^{2}+1}\,j=-4\,i \\ ∇f(2,0) & =\frac{2\cdot 0}{(2)^{2}(0)^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2\cdot 2}{(2)^{2}(0)^{2}+1}\,j=4\,j\end{aligned}
$$
